title: polyframes
description: polybar window-list renderer for herbstluftwm: a bunli/bun CLI compiled to a standalone native binary - rofi menus, typed one-shot window rules, and the WM read as typed JSON via herbstutil; the float-register imperatives come from herbctl.

content.heading: polyframes - the polybar window-list renderer, as a native binary
content: **polyframes** renders **herbstluftwm**'s window state as the **polybar** center module: one label per (frame, window-class) group, decorated by state (focused gold underline, floating, minimized dimmed), with click/scroll actions that re-exec the binary itself.
built with bun and bunli, compiled to a standalone executable - so it runs wherever the bar runs: no node, no nvm PATH, no shim.
[https://github.com/akinevz2/polyframes](https://github.com/akinevz2/polyframes)

content.heading: the bar contract it fills
content: a polybar module owns its slot of the bar: print one formatted line, then keep it fresh. polyframes fills that contract twice over - as a daemon (a `herbstclient --idle` hook listener for instant focus/tag/title updates) and as a one-shot (`polyframes bar` prints a single line and exits - the same pure renderer, scriptable).
the freshness race has one hole: hlwm 0.9.5 emits no hook for frame splits and removals - a 1s layout poll that hashes `herbstclient dump` covers those.

content.heading: the package, architecturally
content: a pure renderer (window state in, one bar line out) under a command layer that manages the dotfiles' whole herbst helper suite as subcommands - one binary, no loose scripts.

clients on the focused tag arrive in WM order, enriched per window: class, title, minimized, floating, and its parent frame's flat index (`-1` when the root is unsplit). group keys: `minflt|wid` and `unframed|wid` are solo labels; `frame|frame|class` groups same-class windows sharing a frame.

two sibling libraries ride along at build time: **herbstutil** (parseAttr for every WM read - typed JSON in one round trip) and **herbctl** (the imperatives the scroll/click actions run: float+center, minimize-keep-frame, empty-frame removal). both resolve as sibling submodules in the doftiles depends/ layout and from the npm/GitHub registries everywhere else.

content.heading: usage - the subcommands
content: `tags`, `hidden`, `windows`, `launch` - the rofi menus (script-mode protocol, NUL-separated rows, per-row icons and states)
`switcher-menu`, `window-menu` - detached menu targets the click actions spawn
`tile` - closest-empty-frame navigation or split (the frame-tree surgery)
`center` - decoration-aware centering (`--wid` targets a specific window's own frame)
`resize` - delta nudges, frame/root deco-flush fills, explicit content rects
`fit` - constraint pass: shrink oversized, nudge off-screen (monitor or frame target)
`spawn` - one-shot `herbstclient rule once` spawns with typed flags (`--class`/`--float`/`--center`/`--tag`)
`bar` - the one-shot renderer line

content.heading: quirks
content: a group's representative is the frame's selected client - but only when it belongs to the group's class, so a mixed-class frame never leaks another group's title.
render order keeps WM order, pushes minimized labels last, truncates to `char_limit` with an ellipsis, folds forbidden classes (the bar itself), and emits a `+N` overflow marker past `max_windows`.

the float-register state machines (mod-f / mod-x / mod-ctrl-f: float-focus, float-yank, zoom) live in **herbctl** - documented in the [**herbctl** project](/projects/herbctl); the polyframes side of the same bindings is the frame surgery: tile/center/resize/fit re-executed in the bar's click actions.

content.heading: stable in v2.x
content: the releases page ships a standalone linux-x64 (glibc) binary - no toolchain, no runtime deps:

```sh
u=https://github.com/akinevz2/polyframes/releases/latest/download
curl -fL $u/polyframes-linux-x64 -o ~/.local/bin/polyframes
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/polyframes
```
the deps resolve through the herbstutil/herbctl split; the help text is terse one-liners that fit polybar's narrow world.
